bull.b: TTM revenue of $58.4M and gross margin above 91% indicate that commercialized antibody products can produce attractive economics. If revenue growth persists, this gross-profit base could help fund development and support operating leverage as scale expands.

Debt of about $8.4M against $181.1M of equity produces debt-to-equity near 0.05, leaving the company conservatively financed. This reduces balance-sheet strain and preserves flexibility to support development or commercialization while losses remain elevated.

LIBERTY Phase 3 produced clinically meaningful, statistically significant safety and tolerability data for VYD2311, while FDA discussions support a planned accelerated-approval BLA. This advances a differentiated prophylaxis candidate toward a regulatory decision and potential commercialization.

bear.b: TTM operating cash flow of about -$108.4M and free cash flow of -$109.7M show that operations are not self-funding. Continued burn alongside large losses can require external financing, potentially consuming capital and limiting strategic flexibility before profitability is reached.

TTM net loss of roughly $107.3M and net margin near -184% outweigh the company’s strong gross margin. Although losses narrowed from 2024 to 2025, they widened again in the TTM period, showing that operating expenses and earnings conversion remain difficult to sustain.

FDA has notified Invivyd that PEMGARDA’s EUA will terminate on June 29, 2027 after the broader COVID EUA declaration ends. The transition creates a defined regulatory gap risk for an existing product and makes a full approval pathway important to preserve access and revenue.
